notes.summary: Algebra in SSC CGL tests algebraic identities, x + 1/x type expressions, three-variable identities, elementary surds, and linear equations with their graphs. Expect 2-4 questions in Tier-I (more in Tier-II) that reward spotting the right identity or substituting easy values instead of expanding long expressions.
keyPoints: (a + b)² = a² + 2ab + b²; (a − b)² = a² − 2ab + b²; a² − b² = (a + b)(a − b); (a + b)² − (a − b)² = 4ab.
(a + b)³ = a³ + b³ + 3ab(a + b); (a − b)³ = a³ − b³ − 3ab(a − b); a³ + b³ = (a + b)(a² − ab + b²).
If x + 1/x = k, then x² + 1/x² = k² − 2 and x³ + 1/x³ = k³ − 3k (x + 1/x = 3 gives x³ + 1/x³ = 27 − 9 = 18). If x − 1/x = k, then x² + 1/x² = k² + 2 and x³ − 1/x³ = k³ + 3k.
A quadratic such as x² − 3x + 1 = 0 becomes x + 1/x = 3 on dividing by x — the standard first move.
a² + b² + c² = (a + b + c)² − 2(ab + bc + ca).
a³ + b³ + c³ − 3abc = (a + b + c)(a² + b² + c² − ab − bc − ca). If a + b + c = 0, then a³ + b³ + c³ = 3abc.
Surds: √(a + 2√b) = √x + √y where x + y = a and xy = b; for example √(5 + 2√6) = √3 + √2. Rationalise 1/(√a − √b) by multiplying by (√a + √b).
Conjugates: if x = 3 + 2√2, then 1/x = 3 − 2√2, so x + 1/x = 6.

The line ax + by = c cuts the x-axis at (c/a, 0) and the y-axis at (0, c/b), and its slope is −a/b. Two lines a1x + b1y = c1 and a2x + b2y = c2 have a unique solution if a1/a2 ≠ b1/b2, no solution if a1/a2 = b1/b2 ≠ c1/c2, and infinitely many if all three ratios are equal.
Value substitution: when an identity must hold for all allowed values, put simple numbers (for example a = 1, b = 3) and test the options.
traps: Using k² − 2 for an x − 1/x problem; with a minus sign it becomes k² + 2.
Writing (a + b)³ = a³ + b³ and dropping the 3ab(a + b) term.
Applying a³ + b³ + c³ = 3abc when a + b + c is not zero.
Confusing √x − 1/√x with √x + 1/√x — square the expression and compare with x + 1/x to see which one is asked.
Forgetting the ½ when finding the area of the triangle a line makes with the axes.
notes.examTip: When the options are numbers but the expression has letters, plug in small values that satisfy the given condition (such as a = 3, b = 5, c = 7) — it is often faster than the algebra.

questions.explanation:
Use a³ + b³ = (a + b)(a² − ab + b²) with a = 0.87 and b = 0.13.
The expression = (a³ + b³) ÷ (a² − ab + b²) = a + b.
= 0.87 + 0.13 = 1.

questions.text: At which point do the graphs of the linear equations 2x + y = 8 and x − y = 1 intersect?
questions.explanation:
Add the two equations: (2x + y) + (x − y) = 8 + 1 → 3x = 9 → x = 3.
Then y = x − 1 = 2.
Check: 2 × 3 + 2 = 8 and 3 − 2 = 1.
The lines intersect at (3, 2).

questions.text: If a + b + c = 9 and ab + bc + ca = 26, what is the value of a² + b² + c²?
If x − 1/x = 4, what is the value of x³ − 1/x³?
questions.explanation:
Use x³ − 1/x³ = (x − 1/x)³ + 3(x − 1/x).
With x − 1/x = 4: 4³ + 3 × 4 = 64 + 12 = 76.
(52 comes from wrongly subtracting 12, which is the rule for x + 1/x.)

questions.text: If x² − 5x + 1 = 0, what is the value of x⁴ + 1/x⁴?

questions.explanation:
Write 7 + 4√3 = 7 + 2√12.
Find two numbers whose sum is 7 and product is 12: 4 and 3.
So 7 + 4√3 = (√4 + √3)² = (2 + √3)².
Hence √(7 + 4√3) = 2 + √3.

questions.text: The line 3x + 4y = 12 meets the x-axis at A and the y-axis at B. What is the area of triangle OAB, where O is the origin?
questions.explanation:
x-intercept: put y = 0 → 3x = 12 → x = 4, so A = (4, 0).
y-intercept: put x = 0 → 4y = 12 → y = 3, so B = (0, 3).
Triangle OAB is right-angled at O: area = ½ × 4 × 3 = 6 sq units.

questions.text: If a + b + c = 0, where a, b and c are non-zero, what is the value of a²/(bc) + b²/(ca) + c²/(ab)?
questions.explanation:
Take the LCM abc: a²/(bc) + b²/(ca) + c²/(ab) = (a³ + b³ + c³) ÷ abc.
When a + b + c = 0, a³ + b³ + c³ = 3abc.
So the value = 3abc ÷ abc = 3.

questions.text: If x = 3 + 2√2, what is the value of √x − 1/√x?
If a + b + c = 15 and a² + b² + c² = 83, what is the value of a³ + b³ + c³ − 3abc?
If x = 4ab/(a + b), where a ≠ b, what is the value of (x + 2a)/(x − 2a) + (x + 2b)/(x − 2b)?
questions.explanation:
x/(2a) = 2b/(a + b). By componendo-dividendo, (x + 2a)/(x − 2a) = (2b + a + b)/(2b − a − b) = (a + 3b)/(b − a).
Similarly x/(2b) = 2a/(a + b) gives (x + 2b)/(x − 2b) = (3a + b)/(a − b).
Sum = [(3a + b) − (a + 3b)] ÷ (a − b) = (2a − 2b) ÷ (a − b) = 2.
Quick check: a = 1, b = 3 gives x = 3, and 5 + (−3) = 2.
